title: Mods and the community list
summary: Add mods to your server and see which ones work with Coop.

sections.heading: Adding mods
steps: Go to Mods and press Add mods.
Tick the mods you want on the server.
Press Save module config, then restart the server.

sections.heading: Adding mods to a running campaign
steps: You can add mods to a campaign that is already going. Turn them on and press Start server.
Start server asks before it loads the save with the new mods, and makes a backup of the save first.
Load backup on Saves puts the save back as it was.
A Restart does not ask again for the same mods.
Turning off a mod the save was made with is refused. Turn it back on, or make a new campaign save.
sections.tip: Keep the old mods in their order and put the new ones under them.

sections.heading: The community list
steps: Every mod has a badge from the community list. It says if the mod works, is broken, is client only or is not tested yet.
Broken mods break Coop games. Leave them off.
Client only mods go on your friends' games, not on the server.
Use the chips above the list to show just one kind.

sections.heading: Testing mods yourself
steps: Press Test mods on the server to try each mod alone on a throwaway campaign.
Your own results show next to the badge, so you know what works on your PC.

sections.heading: RBM settings
steps: When RBM is on in your setup, Settings shows the card RBM settings for this PC's game.
It edits RBM's config.xml on this PC, the file your own game reads when you play from this PC.
Turn RBM's parts and its campaign options on or off there, then press Save RBM settings.
The Coop server does not run RBM's code. RBM's campaign rules run in each player's own game, so every player should use the same values.
Coop friendly turns off Lords buy equipment. That RBM setting empties the town markets in coop.
Coop and Friends turns it off in each player's own game when they press Connect, unless they untick Keep RBM coop friendly.
sections.tip: If the card says RBM has no config.xml yet, play once with RBM on this PC.

sections.heading: Same mods for everyone
steps: Friends need the same mods as the server.
Press Share mod list and send it to them.
To play Coop with no mods at all, pick the Plain Coop (no mods) setup. Friends pick the same setup in Coop and Friends.
sections.tip: Changing the mod list makes Bannerlord build its shaders again, so the first start after a change is slow.
